It actually is what you're looking for.
Changing the size of the game window is not the same as resolution - it makes more of the game map visible, but one pixel is still one pixel.
You're asking to scale the graphics up, as
@Archeia
pointed out, which
is
decreasing the resolution. It's using more than one pixel on the monitor's display to draw one pixel of the game's artwork.
Note that the screen scale option automatically also affects the game window size - if you want to just zoom into the map without affecting the game window or UI, there are a number of plugins available for that.

I don't really understand your example. There are plugins you can use to have larger tiles, but you have to
draw
them that way. It doesn't make anything look bigger.
Default game window size of 816x624
Increasing the game window size to 1920x1080:
Everything is exactly the same size, one pixel in the sprite is displayed with one pixel on your monitor. But the window is larger so you see more (and there's all the black where I didn't draw a map).
Keeping the game window size of 816x624, but increasing the
scale
(the resolution) to 2:
Now everything looks twice as large because you are telling your monitor to use 2x2 pixels to display each pixel from the source image.
